reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73066: AFFECTED, NOT REACHABLE — Tesseract. Heap out-of-bounds WRITE. A crafted .traineddata LSTM component wraps a signed multiplication in Convolve::DeSerialize, undersizing the forward-pass output buffer. Verified present in the vendored 5.5.2 rather than inferred from the CVE's version string: thirdparty/tesseract/src/lstm/convolve.cpp:49 computes `no_ = ni_ * (2 * half_x_ + 1) * (2 * half_y_ + 1)` with no overflow check. Fixed upstream in 5.5.3, which MuPDF 1.28.0 does not vendor. NOT REACHABLE: no shipped code references any OCR door (see reachability.ocr). SECOND boundary when Stage 6 lands: the attacker input here is the MODEL, not the document. It stays unreachable only while .traineddata is shipped by us and neither the language nor the datadir passed to ocr_init is influenced by a document or by user input.
reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73067: AFFECTED, NOT REACHABLE — Tesseract. Heap out-of-bounds READ, crash before image processing. A crafted .traineddata dawg with an unterminated forward-edge run is accepted, after which last_edge walks past edges_. Verified present in the vendored 5.5.2: thirdparty/tesseract/src/dict/dawg.cpp:313-350 checks the magic number and asserts num_edges_ > 0, then reads num_edges_ records and returns true with NO check that the final edge carries the terminator marker; dawg.h:542 then indexes edges_ unchecked. Fixed upstream in 5.5.3. Same reachability and the same model-versus-document boundary as DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73066.

reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2025-55780: NOT-APPLICABLE — the EPUB parser is not in the shipped binary. Re-closed on a mechanism after a period UNDER REVIEW, and the history is the useful part. It was NOT-AFFECTED on the premise 'this application opens PDF; no EPUB path is reachable. Revisit if EPUB import is added (Stage 8)'. Measured 2026-08-18, that premise described a guard that did not exist: mz_open calls fz_open_document, which scores every registered handler against the stream's CONTENT as well as the filename, and the shim's 'not a PDF' refusal comes from pdf_specifics AFTER fz_open_document returns — so a file content-scoring as EPUB was opened and parsed by the EPUB handler before being refused. ADR-0016 names the handler set instead of inheriting it. Build-time -DFZ_ENABLE_EPUB=0 removes the registration, and the linker then discarded the unreferenced objects: handlerFootprint.mjs finds no EPUB marker in the rebuilt DLL where it found application/epub+zip and META-INF/container.xml before, and the binary fell from 42,124,800 to 39,373,824 bytes. The parser is absent, so the advisory does not apply to what ships rather than resting on a claim about reachability. Note the discard was PARTIAL across formats — HTML and Office markers survive, and for those the verdict would rest on non-registration rather than absence; this entry is EPUB and EPUB is gone. proof:documenthandlers holds the reachability half end to end.

reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-7233: NOT-AFFECTED — CORRECTED from an earlier AFFECTED verdict that read the CVE text instead of upstream history. The CVE says "up to 1.28.0", which is the report-time upper bound, not a statement that 1.28.0 ships the bug. The fixing commits — Artifex bug 709364 (missing bounds checks in CFF subsetting) and 709365 — landed 2026-05-13, before 1.28.0 shipped 2026-06-26, and are present in .tools/mupdf/1.28.0: subset-cff.c:299 (data_offset > len) and :315 (data_offset + v > len). Verified by executing the trigger against the built engine: scripts/security/cffOobProof.mjs shows a clean throw with the checks and a crash without them. Additionally NOT REACHABLE: font subsetting is opt-in via pdf_subset_fonts, which no code path we ship calls, and pdf_save_document does not reach it.

watch.ARTIFEX-BUG-709567: UNRESOLVED (no CVE, no release) — "potential memory overwrite in CFF2 subsetting", fixed upstream in commit a3caa67262bd on 2026-08-07. In NO released version: it postdates 1.28.2 (2026-08-03) and exists only on master. A memory OVERWRITE, so more serious than the over-read of CVE-2026-7233. NOT REACHABLE here: CFF2 subsetting requires font subsetting, which no shipped code path performs. Take at the first release that contains it, per ADR-0011; until then the register is the record that it is known and waiting.

ocr.why: Tesseract and Leptonica are statically linked into the shipped DLL, and neither is reachable from any of the shim's 24 exported functions (24 in the source, 24 in the built DLL by dumpbin /EXPORTS — the same names). Presence in the binary is NOT the question and does not settle it: ?AVTessErrStream@tesseract@@ is in the 42 MB DLL because MuPDF's own OCR translation units reference it, which says nothing about whether our code can get there. TWO independent measurements settle it, in opposite directions. (1) No shipped file references any of the symbols below, and those symbols are every public MuPDF function with a call path into ocr_init/ocr_recognise/ocr_fin — derived from the compiled source by scripts/security/ocrDoors.mjs, not written by hand, re-derived on every run. (2) Walking the call graph FORWARD from the 24 exports reaches 5583 functions and not one door (scripts/security/shimReach.mjs). The second measurement exists because the first answers a question about our source text rather than about the binary: it would still read clean if an export reached a door through an intermediate that named it for us. mz_save routes through pdf_save_document, never through the writer dispatch. Both walks carry positive controls that must locate something known-present, because a search's failure modes all look like 'found nothing' — which here is the reassuring answer. Leptonica sits behind the same doors because in this build it is armed from exactly one call site, fz_set_leptonica_mem inside ocr_init. Note fz_new_document_writer: it needs no caller to name an OCR symbol at all, because the writer is chosen from a FILE EXTENSION, so a path ending .ocr reaches Tesseract. FZ_ENABLE_OCR_OUTPUT defaults to 1 and libmupdf.vcxproj's Release|x64 configuration defines HAVE_TESSERACT and HAVE_LEPTONICA, so that dispatch is live in the binary we ship — which is why invariant 23 now bans the dispatcher family from shipped code outright, rather than leaving this as a fact to re-establish at every release. This expires when Stage 6 lands OCR, which is the point: the verdict is about this codebase today, not about the engine.

engine-host-containment.why: Invariant 25 requires every document-parsing process to run at the lowest workable integrity level, under a job object bounding memory and process creation, with NO NETWORK, and with no filesystem reach beyond what it was handed. The hosts do not exist yet — electron is not a dependency and apps/desktop is a bare index.ts — so this is policy before mechanism, declared here so it cannot decay into a note. The day shipped code names utilityProcess or MessageChannelMain, this verdict expires and the build fails naming the invariant. WHAT THIS TRIGGER DOES NOT DO: it catches 'a utility host was written', not 'and it was contained'. It is a prompt to implement, and the thing it prompts is the runtime assertion recorded as a docs/FEATURES.md row — integrity level, job limits and network denial asserted against a RUNNING process, not against the options passed to it. This mechanism is a git grep over path globs (scripts/lib/verdict.mjs), not the C walker that derives the OCR doors, so it reads TypeScript exactly as it reads C — verified against packages/*/src/**.

kernel-error-path-sanitisation.why: Not an engine advisory. It is here because this register is the project's one mechanism for a verdict that expires when the code moves, and rebuilding that mechanism elsewhere is how two hand-rolled copies of one idea get to disagree (scripts/lib/verdict.mjs). THE CLAIM: no filesystem path reaches the renderer through a DocumentService error. THE INPUT ITS TRUTH RESTS ON: no IPC handler calls DocumentService yet. readFileIdentity narrows absence to ENOENT/ENOTDIR and RETHROWS every other errno, which is correct — a catch-all there would be a normaliser wearing a guard's clothes — but a rethrown EACCES is a Node fs error carrying the absolute path in both .message and .path, and it escapes open() to whoever called it. The kernel is the right place to throw honestly and the boundary is the right place to sanitise (ADR-0009 §9), so today's claim holds only because apps/desktop/src is a bare index.ts. It stops holding on the day the first handler is written, and that day is a routine feature commit that will not prompt anyone to re-read the ADR. WHAT THIS TRIGGER DOES NOT DO: it catches 'a handler reached DocumentService', not 'and its errors were sanitised'. It is a prompt to implement, and the thing it prompts is the docs/FEATURES.md row for the sanitising boundary — errors mapped to structured failures carrying no path, proven by a control that asserts a path DOES appear when the mapping is removed. Passing this red requires recording a new verdict that names the boundary, which is the point: mechanical rather than remembered. Scoped to apps/*/src/** because the kernel obviously names its own class and apps/desktop is the only package that can register an ipcMain handler.

pdf_subset_fonts.why: Font subsetting is opt-in in MuPDF. fz_subset_cff_for_gids is reached only through pdf_subset_fonts, which pdf_save_document does not call and no shipped path invokes. This is what makes both verdicts NOT REACHABLE — and it is a claim about THIS codebase, not about the engine. Optimise and export are exactly the features that will call it, and 709567 is a memory OVERWRITE that no release fixes, so enabling subsetting inherits a live one.

reachabilityControl.why: Every verdict above is a SEARCH, and a search reports 'no references' for every way it can be broken — a glob matching no files, a symbol misspelt here, git grep run from the wrong root. All of them look exactly like the answer everyone hoped for. So the walk must first find something it is known to find, per path glob, on every run (audit item 4b). This symbol is the shim's single registration call site (ADR-0016, invariant 23): it is present by construction and its disappearance would itself be worth stopping on.

The control proving packages/*/src/** resolves. A control over native/** says nothing about whether this glob matches any files, and pdf_subset_fonts and engine-host-containment both rest on it being scanned. CapabilityRegistry is the oldest class in packages/kernel and is named by its own module, its test and the kernel index.

The control proving apps/*/src/** resolves, and the one that matters most: kernel-error-path-sanitisation scans ONLY this glob, so a glob that matched nothing would leave that verdict permanently, silently green. apps/desktop/src/index.ts is a bare 'export {};' today, which leaves 'export' as the only stable token in it — weak as a symbol and exactly right as a control, because what is being controlled for is whether any file under this glob is read at all.
